items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently upheld the constitutional validity of amendments made in 2010 to the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, that regulate constructions in areas surrounding centrally protected monuments [ BR Ramakrishna v. Union of India & others ]. By an October 9 ruling, Justice MGS Kamal rejected a challenge to Sections 20A, 20B and 20C of the Act by Tumkur resident BR Ramakrishna, who contended that the restrictions on construction within prohibited areas were arbitrary and unconstitutional. “Considering the object and purport of the Act and the constitutional mandate of Article 49 (protecting monuments) of the Constitution of India said classification cannot be found to be unreasonable, ambiguous or vague and unconnected as sought to be contended by the counsel for the petitioner. In any event, the reason and logic behind such classification falls within the expert domain of concerned competent authority under the Act, 1958," the Court held. items.title: The void marriage and the invisible widow: Why the law needs an equitable answer
items.summary: A woman can spend her adult life with a man, raise his children, run his household and give up her career, and still walk away with nothing the day he dies, because a court later finds the marriage void. This recurs whenever a marriage falls foul of Section 5, read with Section 11, of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA). The woman never becomes a wife in the eyes of law, so she can never become a widow either. And the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 (HSA) has no room for her. The answer is not to pretend the marriage was valid. It lies in something the HMA already accepts: that the legal fate of a relationship and its economic consequences need not be tied together. Section 16 legitimises children of void and voidable marriages without validating the marriage. The same idea can be extended, carefully and narrowly, to the woman who lived the marriage in good faith. The statutory bind Section 5(i) requires that neither party have a living spouse at the time of marriage. Section 11 declares a marriage in breach void from inception (Section 12 covers voidable marriages), so the woman never becomes a wife. items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said that a strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government but one which allows its citizens to question the government. At a time when democratic institutions across the world are facing challenges, young lawyers and policymakers have a special responsibility to protect the Constitution and uphold democratic values, he opined. “A strong democracy must allow its citizens to question the government. A strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government. It is one where every citizen has the freedom to question the government. Never stop questioning, never compromise on your values and never forget the people,” he said. Shivakumar was addressing graduating students at the 34th convocation ceremony of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) at the Jnana Jyothi Auditorium in Bengaluru. items.title: Detained on arrival: Section 172 BNSS and the borrowed power to stop a protest
items.summary: On October 10, 2026, a protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar was supposed to take place. For many who set out to participate in this protest, the trip was cut short on the railway platform itself. People travelling to Delhi for the protest were reportedly detained in several States before they even reached the capital. In Madhya Pradesh, at least 30 people were taken off trains and were detained at Bhopal, Gwalior and Itarsi . In Delhi itself, the police had imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which bars assemblies of five or more, processions and dharnas without prior written permission. None of this is new. What is new is the provision the State now uses to justify it. When the Uttarakhand High Court asked, in July, under what law an activist on his way to an earlier protest at Jantar Mantar had been taken off a train at Rishikesh, the State’s answer was Section 172 of the BNSS. items.title: The long wait: What 24 Supreme Court references reveal about judicial delay
items.summary: In February 2002, seven judges of the Supreme Court were asked whether a citizen’s private property counts as a “material resource of the community” that the State may redistribute under Article 39(b). The Court said it had “some difficulty” with an older ruling answering the question in the affirmative and sent the question to nine judges. Those nine judges first sat on April 23, 2024. The judgment in Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra was pronounced on November 5, 2024. 22 years and nine months to get a hearing. Six-and-a-half months to decide. I wanted to know whether that was unusual, so I counted. I collected every question the Supreme Court sent to a bench of seven or more judges that was decided, or was still waiting, between January 2000 and September 30, 2026. There are 24. items.title: Courting Controversy: Green becomes the new Gold: India’s Carbon Market opens for business
items.summary: As Diwali approaches and Delhi braces for its annual smog season, conversations about air quality usually turn to firecrackers and stubble burning. These conversations seem to miss out on pollution caused by factories, power plants and furnaces that run all year and are a steadier source of pollution. This is a fitting moment to ask what India’s biggest industrial emitters have been doing, and how the 2026 UN Climate Change COP31 will bring about an environmental change for the better. Starting November, for the first time, Indian factories will be able to buy and sell carbon credit certificates on power exchanges, finally turning a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified by the government in 2023, into a working market reality. The legal foundation for the concept is the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022, which empowered the government to create an Indian carbon market and a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified in 2023 . The Bureau of Energy Efficiency has issued emission targets to around 490 industrial units across seven sectors and credits are expected to be issued this month, with trading between November and January. items.title: UAPA no blanket bar on foreign travel: Delhi High Court allows riots accused Natasha Narwal to go to UK for PhD
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has allowed Delhi riots accused Natasha Narwal to travel to the United Kingdom for academic purposes and to meet her PhD supervisors. Justice Amit Bansal passed the order on October 16 and set aside the trial court order of October 6, which had denied her permission. While passing the order, the Court said that a case under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) will not act as a blanket bar on a person's right to travel abroad. “The fact that the petitioner has been charged of serious offences under the UAPA does not curtail her right to travel abroad in a blanket manner,” the High Court observed in its order. Therefore, the Court allowed her to travel on a personal bond of ₹1 lakh with her brother as surety. Justice Bansal further said she will not seek asylum in the UK or comment on the cases against her. Justice Amit Bansal Narwal is pursuing PhD from University of Warwick and sought permission to attend an international academic conference in London, where her research paper, Gendered Carceral Labour as Social Reproduction, has been accepted for presentation.
